entities.summary: The Constitution of Portugal, officially the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic, is the supreme law of Portugal. Approved on 2 April 1976 and becoming effective on 25 April of the same year, it superseded the Estado Novo's 1933 Constitution after the Carnation Revolution. The 1976 Constitution has been amended or revised seven times since its ratification, in 1982, 1989, 1992, 1997, 2001, 2004 and 2005.
